verificationPatterns.pattern: CR adopts next-job voltage when station skips print but downstream job requires ink from station
verificationPatterns.example: CR gets the next job voltage values

verificationPatterns.pattern: Tooltip appears on icon click with relevant error info
verificationPatterns.example: Clicking each icon displays a tooltip with relevant error information.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ignore option is conditionally present based on mismatch type
verificationPatterns.example: The substrate mismatch tooltip includes an 'Ignore' option. The ink mismatch tooltip does NOT include an 'Ignore' option.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Job properties side panel shows same availability icon and tooltip as management screen
verificationPatterns.example: The tooltip matches the one displayed in the job management screen.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Side panel icon click highlights the error area within job properties
verificationPatterns.example: Clicking the icon highlights the error area.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Availability icon disappears after issue is resolved and saved
verificationPatterns.example: After resolving the issue and saving, the availability icon disappears.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Resolved job becomes available for printing
verificationPatterns.example: The job becomes available for printing.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Top-of-queue job with availability issue is indicated in red
verificationPatterns.example: The availability issue is highlighted in red for the job at the top of the list.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Initial mismatch severity is low when next queued job has an availability issue
verificationPatterns.example: The next job in the queue displays an availability issue. The availability issue severity is initially low.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Severity escalates to red when currently printing job has approximately 15 minutes remaining
verificationPatterns.example: When the current printing job shows approximately 15 minutes remaining for completion, verify the severity of the availability issue in the next job. The availability severity of the next job has increased from low to a higher level - Red indication

verificationPatterns.pattern: Continuous mode stops and shows 'no available jobs' indicator when next job has an availability issue
verificationPatterns.example: The system stops printing because the next job has an availability issue, despite being in continuous mode. The system displays an indication that there are 'no_available_printing' jobs.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mismatch severity resets to low (yellow icon) when job is moved from print queue to held queue
verificationPatterns.example: The mismatch severity displayed in the held queue and updated to severity low (Yellow ICON) despite the severity in print queue.

verificationPatterns.pattern: New job added to print queue inherits mismatch severity based on remaining time of currently printing job
verificationPatterns.example: The mismatch severity of the new job is updated to reflect the remaining time of the job currently printing.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Repositioning a job to the bottom of the print queue while press is stopped resets severity to low
verificationPatterns.example: If the press is stopped and the user reposition the job in the bottom of list the severity will be low.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ink coverage aggregation formula
verificationPatterns.example: DFE sends ink coverage per separation via SMJobEntity; press sums all participating separations when CoverageStatus indicates completion; white ink separation is multiplied by 1.7 before summing; total is compared against OneBlanketRotationInkCoverageThreshold (one rotation) and TwoBlanketRotationsInkCoverageThreshold (two rotations); each rotation is individually capped by the single-rotation threshold.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Unavailability triggered on threshold breach
verificationPatterns.example: When total ink coverage exceeds the allowed maximum, the JobExceededAllowedCoverage unavailability is raised and the job appears unavailable in the job management screen.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Unavailability cleared by user disabling separations
verificationPatterns.example: User opens job properties → separations tab → disables one or more separations until recalculated coverage is below threshold → saves; JobExceededAllowedCoverage unavailability is removed and job becomes available for printing.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mismatch indication in separations tab
verificationPatterns.example: When JobExceededAllowedCoverage is active, a visible mismatch indication is displayed in the separations tab of job properties.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Press message content on ink coverage mismatch
verificationPatterns.example: Clicking the ink coverage mismatch icon shows press message: "Ink separations coverage exceeds the allowed limit. Modify job properties to lower ink coverage."

verificationPatterns.pattern: Unavailability signal triggered on resource mismatch
verificationPatterns.example: Verify that the JobNotAvailableScreenNotInstalled unavailability is triggered.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Job marked unavailable with mismatch icon in job management screen
verificationPatterns.example: The job is marked as unavailable. Icon of screen mismatch is display.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Job becomes available for printing after mismatch resolved
verificationPatterns.example: Verify that the job becomes available for printing.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mismatch indication shown inline next to mismatched property field in job properties
verificationPatterns.example: Click on side panel on screen mismatch. Verify that an indication of the mismatch is given next to the screen property field.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Threshold comparison check
verificationPatterns.example: Verify the SW calculates required blanket rotations and compares against MaximumNumberOfRotations

verificationPatterns.pattern: Unavailability flag triggered on threshold breach
verificationPatterns.example: Verify JobExceededAllowedBlanketRotations unavailability is triggered when job exceeds MaximumNumberOfRotations

verificationPatterns.pattern: Job management screen reflects unavailability with icon
verificationPatterns.example: Verify job is marked as unavailable for printing and icon is displayed to user

verificationPatterns.pattern: Unavailability cleared after user remediation
verificationPatterns.example: Modify separations to reduce rotations below MaximumNumberOfRotations, save, verify JobExceededAllowedBlanketRotations is removed and job becomes available

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mismatch indication visible in job properties UI
verificationPatterns.example: Open job properties > separations tab, verify clear indication of blanket rotations mismatch is displayed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Print button disabled with NO_AVAILABLE_JOBS unavailability on ink mismatch
verificationPatterns.example: Verify the print button is disabled (Phase 1) and there is _NO_AVAILABLE_JOBS_ unavailability on print button.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mismatch icon shows correct title and press message key, with no ignore toggle
verificationPatterns.example: Verify icon of INK mismatch appears with Title: 'Ink mismatch', Job availability text (press message): 'JobNotAvailableInkIssue'. The ignore icon is NOT as ignore display.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Single ink unavailability message format: name + status
verificationPatterns.example: The following ink is required for job definitions but is not available: {inkName} - {inkStatus}. Param: Not installed / Deactivated

verificationPatterns.pattern: Multiple inks unavailability message format: bracketed list of name-status pairs
verificationPatterns.example: The following inks are required for job but are not available: [{inkName} - {inkStatus}, {inkName} - {inkStatus}, ...]. Example: Green(not installed), Violet(deactivated).

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ink mismatch indication appears in job properties next to ink separation property field
verificationPatterns.example: Indication of mismatch shall also be given in job properties next to ink separation property field.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Clicking ink mismatch icon shows tooltip and auto-scrolls job properties to separation section
verificationPatterns.example: Click on ink icon and ensure tooltip appear and the job properties automatically move to separation section.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Unavailability clears after resolution (install missing ink OR remove separation from job properties OR reactivate deactivated ink)
verificationPatterns.example: Once the issue is fixed the availability indication disappears (=job can be printed).

verificationPatterns.pattern: Cross-job impact: verify other jobs with differing ink definitions also show unavailability
verificationPatterns.example: Verify availability issues in other jobs that the ink definition in job properties is different than the installed ink.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check unavailability signal fires
verificationPatterns.example: Verify that the JobIlsAvailabilityIssue unavailability is triggered

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check job marked unavailable in job management screen
verificationPatterns.example: Verify that the job is marked as unavailable in the job management screen

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check UI icon displayed for mismatch
verificationPatterns.example: Icon is displayed to user; Click on ILS Mismatch ICON

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check job prints without ILS tools when mismatch ignored

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check ILS mismatch indication in job properties PQ tools tab
verificationPatterns.example: Open the job properties. Navigate to the PQ tools tab. Verify that an indication of the ILS mismatch is given.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check press message param matches ILS fault state
verificationPatterns.example: Press message param should be Deactivated / Not Calibrated / Not Ready depending on ILS fault. Template: 'However, there is an ILS issue: [param1]. If ignored, job will print without ILS tools.'

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check non-white substrate press messages against reference table
verificationPatterns.example: Go over table and ensure press message displays to user as defined in SWR (separate tables for with/without white ink installed)

verificationPatterns.pattern: Print button disabled with specific unavailability code when prerequisite not met
verificationPatterns.example: Verify the print button is disabled (Phase 1) and there is _NO_AVAILABLE_JOBS_ unavailability on print button.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mismatch icon shows expected title, press message key, and sub-toggle label
verificationPatterns.example: Verify icon appears with Title: 'SPM is not available', Job availability text: 'Job__Spm__AvailabilityIssue', Text under ignore toggle: 'Job will be printed without CCC.'

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mismatch indication mirrors into job properties next to the relevant property field
verificationPatterns.example: Verify indication of mismatch shall also be given in job properties next to CCC checkbox property field.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ignore toggle icon visually differs between off and on states
verificationPatterns.example: Verify the ignore icon is NOT as ignore display (toggle off); Verify the ignore icon is as ignore display (toggle on).

verificationPatterns.pattern: Enabling ignore toggle removes the print availability issue
verificationPatterns.example: Switch on the ignore toggle; Verify the Print availability issue does not exist.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ignore mismatch control disabled during active print
verificationPatterns.example: Verify during printing the 'ignore mismatch control' is disabled.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ignore setting persists when job stops before completion
verificationPatterns.example: Stop the job before it was fully printed; The job does not remove the ignore selection.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ignore setting resets after job fully printed, manually removed, or DFE-Press disconnection
verificationPatterns.example: Print all copies of job or remove from press manually or automatically as part of DFE-Press disconnection; Ignore setting shall be reset after the conditions.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Resolving root cause (job property change) clears availability indication
verificationPatterns.example: Remove the CCC definition in job properties; Once the issue is fixed the availability indication disappears (=job can be printed).

verificationPatterns.pattern: Print button disabled with specific unavailability reason on mismatch
verificationPatterns.example: Verify the print button is disabled (Phase 1) and there is _NO_AVAILABLE_JOBS_ unavailability on print button.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mismatch icon shows exact title, press message key, and sub-text
verificationPatterns.example: Title: 'Substrate Mismatch'; Job availability text (press message): 'JobSubstrateNotInstalled'; Text under ignore toggle: 'Job will be printed on installed substrate.'

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mismatch indication also appears inline in job properties next to the relevant field
verificationPatterns.example: Verify indication of mismatch shall also be given in job properties next to substrate property field.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ignore icon reflects correct visual state (non-ignore vs ignore display)
verificationPatterns.example: The ignore icon is NOT as ignore display (before toggle on); verify the ignore icon is as 'ignore display' (after toggle on).

verificationPatterns.pattern: Enabling ignore toggle removes print availability issue
verificationPatterns.example: Verify the Print availability issue does not exist after switching on the ignore toggle.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ignore control is disabled during active printing
verificationPatterns.example: Verify during printing the 'ignore mismatch control' is disabled.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ignore selection persists after job stop or partial print; resets after defined conditions
verificationPatterns.example: The job does not remove the ignore selection [after stop/partial print]. Ignore setting shall be reset after the conditions.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Availability indication disappears once the underlying issue is resolved
verificationPatterns.example: Once the issue is fixed the availability indication disappears (=job can be printed).

verificationPatterns.pattern: Cross-job verification: check other jobs with same substrate mismatch condition
verificationPatterns.example: Verify availability issues in other jobs that the substrate definition in job properties is different than the installed substrate.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Duration counting scope — only PRINTING state counts, Pre/Post-print excluded
verificationPatterns.example: calibration duration counting will start from Press PRINTING state and will finish at the end of printing (Pre/Pos print duration not included and should not count)

verificationPatterns.pattern: UI element appears on state transition — progress + estimation shown when press enters PRINTING state
verificationPatterns.example: when press state changing to Print State, calibration print progress duration appears with calibration duration estimation beside the calibration print progress

verificationPatterns.pattern: Per-calibration expected duration validation — compare actual elapsed time against table reference

verificationPatterns.pattern: Re-run reset behavior — re-calibration restarts duration counter from zero
verificationPatterns.example: in case user re-calibrate the time start from the beginning

verificationPatterns.pattern: Ink mismatch raises availability issue and blocks job from printing
verificationPatterns.example: JOB_INK_MISMATCH - availability issue shall be raised and the job not be available for print

verificationPatterns.pattern: Substrate mismatch raises availability issue and blocks job from printing
verificationPatterns.example: JOB_SUBSTRATE_MISMATCH - availability issue shall be raised and the job not be available for print

verificationPatterns.pattern: SW sends statistics message on secondary screen disconnection
verificationPatterns.example: disconnect one of the secondary screens on press → SW shall indicate this and send statistics press message

verificationPatterns.pattern: UI indication when screens reconnected to different graphics card port

verificationPatterns.pattern: Runtime PE screen disconnection on Standby detected with non-blocking notification

verificationPatterns.pattern: Physical connectivity check

verificationPatterns.pattern: Configuration file existence and match check
verificationPatterns.example: configuration file exist and match to the current monitors configuration

verificationPatterns.pattern: Post-upgrade state preservation check
verificationPatterns.example: SW upgrade end successfully and monitors configuration saved from previous version

verificationPatterns.pattern: Multi-configuration coverage via repetition
verificationPatterns.example: Repeat for different monitors configuration — SW upgrade end successfully and monitors configuration saved from previous version

verificationPatterns.pattern: Manual edit option available in config file
verificationPatterns.example: User shall have an option to edit manually the configuration file

verificationPatterns.pattern: Default mode is automatic
verificationPatterns.example: The default option for setting up the screens shall be automatic setup

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mode change reflected in active mode indicator
verificationPatterns.example: Manual mode active for monitors due to change in the default configuration

verificationPatterns.pattern: Restore-to-default returns to auto mode
verificationPatterns.example: Auto mode active for monitors (Default); the operator screen show the full UI as expected

verificationPatterns.pattern: Hardware change detection — disconnect
verificationPatterns.example: Disconnect one screen; verify all possible screens detected and configured

verificationPatterns.pattern: Hard cap on configured count
verificationPatterns.example: Connect more than 3 screens; verify only 3 are configured regardless

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mode switch assertion
verificationPatterns.example: Switch to manual; verify Manual mode active

verificationPatterns.pattern: UI tool accessibility — multiple entry points
verificationPatterns.example: Tool accessible from pressUI and independently when pressUI did not load

verificationPatterns.pattern: Swap behavior on duplicate selection
verificationPatterns.example: Select screen already assigned to another output; previously assigned screen moves to freed slot

verificationPatterns.pattern: Apply button availability reason on invalid state
verificationPatterns.example: Define disconnected screen in tool; Apply button disabled with relevant availability reason

verificationPatterns.pattern: UI reflects physical screen count
verificationPatterns.example: Connect 2 screens; UI tool shows only 2 monitors configured to relevant area

verificationPatterns.pattern: Cancel exits without applying changes
verificationPatterns.example: Click Cancel; tool closes and monitor setup stops

verificationPatterns.pattern: Hardware wiring verification against diagram
verificationPatterns.example: Verify all monitors connected as required [confluence wiring diagram link]

verificationPatterns.pattern: OS display mode assertion

verificationPatterns.pattern: Threshold-triggered UI notification

verificationPatterns.pattern: Wizard UI element state validation
verificationPatterns.example: Title is 'WHS Relative Speed Calibration'; substrate name matches installed; Play button inactive with tooltip 'Press state Ready required'; Close button active

verificationPatterns.pattern: Availability tied to press state/tension
verificationPatterns.example: Play button unavailable with tooltip 'Web tension required' when tension released in UW or RW

verificationPatterns.pattern: User-stopped calibration leaves values unchanged
verificationPatterns.example: After Stop during Print state: press returns to Dynamic Ready, Recalibrate button appears, 'The calibration was stopped by the user' displayed, all gear ratio values remain unchanged

verificationPatterns.pattern: Forced-failure via PLC parameter injection with status code verification
verificationPatterns.example: Set ItmTrqHighLim=1 and ItmTrqLowLim=0.1; expect WhsSpeedCalibStatus=3 (Failed), WhsSpeedCalibFailReason=4 (Ref_torque_is_out_of_range), red bar in UI, gear ratio values unchanged

verificationPatterns.pattern: Successful calibration updates all gear ratio signal layers
verificationPatterns.example: Set ItmTrqHighLim=70 and ItmTrqLowLim=-30; expect WhsSpeedCalibStatus=4, green bar, and APP/PLC imported/PLC saved/PLC current gear ratio values all updated to new values

verificationPatterns.pattern: Monitor warning with threshold and value presentation in press message
verificationPatterns.example: BLANKET_TORQUE_MONITORING_HIGH event issued; press message contains ItmAvgTorqueAtEng, ItmAvgTorqueAtDisEng, ItmAvgTorque values plus torque difference limit; press state unchanged; printing continues

verificationPatterns.pattern: Pre/post-upgrade signal value snapshot comparison
verificationPatterns.example: All the values should be equal after successful calibration.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Calibration parameter persistence across SW upgrade
verificationPatterns.example: Gear ratio should be consistent during SW upgrade.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Kibana index query: confirm calibration records visible under time-ranged index
verificationPatterns.example: In Discover tab select whs-relative*, choose correct time — all calibration results should appear

verificationPatterns.pattern: Kibana event payload field check: assert required fields present in named report event
verificationPatterns.example: Verify WhsRelativeSpeedCalibrationReport was sent, including: WhsSpeedCalibStatus, GearRatioInUse, GearRatioResults, SubstrateName, SubstrateThickness, ImpPressure

verificationPatterns.pattern: Kibana Events dashboard: assert named event fired with required telemetry fields after session end
verificationPatterns.example: Verify BLANKET_TORQUE_MONITOR_HIGH event was sent, including: ItmTorqueMonitoringAvgT2DisEngage, ItmTorqueMonitoringAvgT2Engage

verificationPatterns.pattern: Feature inactive during calibration prints
verificationPatterns.example: Print a calibration (Color Calibration or Scaling) — no press message regarding ITM torque difference is issued

verificationPatterns.pattern: Warning fires only after web starts moving, not in Pre-Print state
verificationPatterns.example: ITM torque high difference warning should appear in UI only when web starts moving, not in Pre-Print state

verificationPatterns.pattern: Deduplication: exactly one press message per print session (per Play press)
verificationPatterns.example: Only one press message appears per print session (once after each Play button is hit)

verificationPatterns.pattern: Event payload contains required diagnostic fields
verificationPatterns.example: BLANKET_TORQUE_MONITORING_HIGH event includes: ItmTorqueMonitoringAvgT2DisEngage, ItmTorqueMonitoringAvgT2Engage, ItmTorqueMonitoringDelta, ItmTorqueMonitoringDeltaLimit, GearRatioInUse, Substrate Name, Substrate Thickness, Impression Pressure

verificationPatterns.pattern: Bypass signal disables monitoring entirely
verificationPatterns.example: Set ItmTorqueMonitoringBypass = True, print user job — ITM torque monitor is OFF

verificationPatterns.pattern: Wizard failure UI state: red line, failure label, and Recalibrate button replace Play button
verificationPatterns.example: Red line appears in the top of the wizard dialogue. 'Not Completed'/'Calibration Failed' red text appears under the Play button. Play button changes to Recalibrate button, with Recalibrate text under it. Recalibrate button is available. Close button is available.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Gear ratio signals unchanged after any failure or stop
verificationPatterns.example: Current gear ratio values were not changed in: gInterface.Web.Ctrl.In.Par.Save.GearRatio_arr and gInterface.Web.Comp.WHS.Ctrl.In.Par.Local.StartStop.UnitsToLinearFactorRegular

verificationPatterns.pattern: OPCUA calibration status set to Stopped after any failure or stop
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.WEB.ExportedData.WHS.Calibrations.SpeedCalib.WhsSpeedCalibStatus = Stopped

verificationPatterns.pattern: Kibana statistics report sent after every failure with mandatory fields
verificationPatterns.example: Search for 'whs-relative-speed-calibration' in Kibana. Report must include: Current time and Date, Old GR = gInterface.Web.Ctrl.In.Par.Save.GearRatio_arr, Test result: Failure, Failure reason: <reason-code>

verificationPatterns.pattern: Error dialog appears only after third consecutive calibration failure
verificationPatterns.example: After 3 consecutive calibration failures error message appears: Title 'WHS relative speed calibration failure', Event WHS_RELATIVE_SPEED_CALIBRATION_MAX_RETRIES_RERACHED

verificationPatterns.pattern: Inject out-of-range limit to trigger specific algorithmic failure reason
verificationPatterns.example: Set gInterface.Web.Comp.WHS.Ctrl.In.Par.Local.SpeedCalibration.GearRatioHighLim a bit smaller than current gear ratio to force Failure reason: GearRatioIsOutOfRange

verificationPatterns.pattern: Inject external non-wizard fault to trigger external interrupt failure
verificationPatterns.example: Set OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.IMO.HW_Inputs.Reservoir.ImoRtnBfrVol.Value = 18 while wizard is running; release value after failure; verify press returns to Ready and error message appears in UI

verificationPatterns.pattern: Post-wizard job print confirms gear ratio was never persisted
verificationPatterns.example: Print arbitrary user job. Gear ratio (gInterface.Web.Comp.WHS.Ctrl.In.Par.Local.StartStop.UnitsToLinearFactorRegular) equals value saved in the beginning of the test.

verificationPatterns.pattern: GearRatioResult exported signal captures computed (rejected) calibration output
verificationPatterns.example: Calibration result (OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.WEB.ExportedData.WHS.Calibrations.SpeedCalib.GearRatioResult) included in statistics report

verificationPatterns.pattern: Revert all injected limit overrides at end of test
verificationPatterns.example: Revert all changed limits to correct values (Step 11)

verificationPatterns.pattern: Wizard initial appearance check
verificationPatterns.example: Title is 'WHS Relative Speed Calibration'; substrate name matches installed substrate; Play button active; calibration-time warning displayed; Close button active

verificationPatterns.pattern: Signal baseline snapshot before action
verificationPatterns.example: Save values of all 5 gear-ratio signals before starting calibration so post-action comparison is possible

verificationPatterns.pattern: User-abort leaves signals unchanged
verificationPatterns.example: Press Play then Stop; verify all 5 gear-ratio signals equal saved baseline; UI shows red 'Calibration stopped by the user' with X icon; Stop→Replay/Recalibrate; Close active; press returns to Ready/Dynamic ready

verificationPatterns.pattern: In-progress UI state check
verificationPatterns.example: After pressing Replay: Play→Stop; infinite progress animation around Stop button; Close button not active

verificationPatterns.pattern: Mid-calibration signal invariant
verificationPatterns.example: At calibration start: gInterface.Web.Comp.WHS.Ctrl.In.Par.Local.StartStop.UnitsToLinearFactorRegular = OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.WEB.ImportedData.WHS.Param.SpeedGearRatio.Value; gInterface.Web.Ctrl.In.Par.Save.UnitsToLinearFactorRegular unchanged

verificationPatterns.pattern: Calibration success UI + signal update

verificationPatterns.pattern: Calibrated value active during print
verificationPatterns.example: Print user job on calibrated substrate; verify all 5 gear-ratio signals reflect new calibration value

verificationPatterns.pattern: Signal persistence across PLC and APP restart
verificationPatterns.example: Close wizard; close press SW; HW restart (PLC off then on); relaunch SW; verify all 5 gear-ratio signals still hold calibration value from successful run

verificationPatterns.pattern: Verify charge state after controlled stop
verificationPatterns.example: Stop printing → Verify that ASIDS charged 10 V after printing stopped

verificationPatterns.pattern: Verify charge retention event after fault injection
verificationPatterns.example: Simulate PLC crush → Verify that ASID remain charged event generated; if event absent, check if ASIDS charged; if charged, open defect

verificationPatterns.pattern: Conditional defect gate on missing event
verificationPatterns.example: If ASID remain charged event not generated, check ASIDS charge state; if still charged without event → open defect

verificationPatterns.pattern: Signal equals calibrated GearRatio array entry for installed substrate thickness when web starts to move
verificationPatterns.example: 90 um substrate → gInterface.Web.Comp.WHS.Ctrl.In.Par.Local.StartStop.UnitsToLinearFactorRegular = gInterface.Web.Ctrl.In.Par.Save.GearRatio_arr[3]; 150 um substrate → GearRatio_arr[5]

verificationPatterns.pattern: Signal equals hardcoded default value for substrate with no calibrated gear ratio entry
verificationPatterns.example: 110 um substrate (uncalibrated) → gInterface.Web.Comp.WHS.Ctrl.In.Par.Local.StartStop.UnitsToLinearFactorRegular = 0.1265

verificationPatterns.pattern: Same gear ratio index applies for both user job and color calibration prints on the same substrate
verificationPatterns.example: 150 um: user job → GearRatio_arr[5]; color calibration → GearRatio_arr[5]

verificationPatterns.pattern: Boolean completion flag check
verificationPatterns.example: Verify PostPrintPhase1Done = True

verificationPatterns.pattern: State transition sequence: GoTo command followed by final state arrival
verificationPatterns.example: Verify CR GoToReady and then to Ready state

verificationPatterns.pattern: Engagement state assertion after transition

verificationPatterns.pattern: Timed wait for async sub-process completion
verificationPatterns.example: Wait Up To 10 minutes for ASID cleaning

verificationPatterns.pattern: Component at named operational state
verificationPatterns.example: Verify ASID at Post Print; Verify ASID Drive at standby; Verify ME station at Ready

verificationPatterns.pattern: Conductance failure boundary simulation — verify correct cutout signal fires for each ICR/IBR ratio threshold crossing
verificationPatterns.example: Simulate (ICR-IBR)/ICR > AllowedConductanceLimit && (IBR-ICR)/ICR <= AllowedConductanceLimit → expect CRG_BR_CHARGIN_CONDUCTANCE_IS_FAILED_CUTOUT; swap condition → expect CRG_CR_CHARGIN_CONDUCTANCE_IS_FAILED_CUTOUT

verificationPatterns.pattern: ASID voltage ramp with P.S. feedback tolerance check at each setpoint
verificationPatterns.example: Charge ASID base to ASIDbaseDefaultPrintVoltage; wait PsStabTime; verify P.S. feedback voltage error <= ChargingThreshold; repeat for ASIDVdcDefaultDischargeVoltage - 10V

verificationPatterns.pattern: Soft engage precondition guard — check CrDisengageRequired flag and enforce disengage order before engage when timeout elapsed
verificationPatterns.example: If CrDisengageRequired is TRUE (SoftEngegeTimeOut 60s passed since last disengage), verify disengage order sent before CR engage

verificationPatterns.pattern: Short circuit test sequence at engage — activate test, verify ASID voltage target, then confirm flag cleared
verificationPatterns.example: Activate ShortCircuit test; verify ASID charged to ASIDVdcDefaultDischargeVoltage - 10V; verify CrAtEngageShortCircuitTestRequired = False

verificationPatterns.pattern: Conductance diagnostics dual-sweep — set VDC/VBR alternately to 500V/0V and 0V/500V, sample ICR and IBR at configured rate and iteration count
verificationPatterns.example: Set VdcVoltageConductanceSet=500V, VbrVoltageConductanceSet=0V; measure ICR/IBR per ChargingConductanceSampleRate × ChargingConductanceSampleIteration; then swap voltages; restore AsidVdcDefaultDischargeVoltage

verificationPatterns.pattern: Post-ready ASID residual charge check — after disengage and return to ready mode verify ASID settles to expected low voltage
verificationPatterns.example: Disengage CR; verify after getting ready mode ASID is charged 10V

verificationPatterns.pattern: Post-update print job execution
verificationPatterns.example: Print job from DFE → Job from DFE printed.

verificationPatterns.pattern: For each parameter in XML startup list, verify matching entry exists in HW solution driver start-up list tab with identical index and data
verificationPatterns.example: Open EH_AIR_KNF_BLWR.Xml, locate 'Motor Rated Frequency', confirm index and data match corresponding entry in HW solution

verificationPatterns.pattern: Convert XML hex index to HW solution format: strip leading zeros and prepend '0x' to the register portion (e.g., XML hex 8197 -> 0x2005, matches HW solution display 2005:06)
verificationPatterns.example: XML index 8197 (hex) = 0x2005 (DEC) corresponds to HW solution index 2005:06

verificationPatterns.pattern: Repeat parameter/index/data comparison exhaustively for all parameters in the startup list file
verificationPatterns.example: Do this step to all parameters

verificationPatterns.pattern: Failure event display with subsystem attribution
verificationPatterns.example: Relevant subsystem displayed; failure display on UI for the relevant subsystem

verificationPatterns.pattern: Severity passthrough from BL to ES and history reports
verificationPatterns.example: ES and all history reports shall receive the severity as it was classified by BL

verificationPatterns.pattern: All event parameters present on failure event
verificationPatterns.example: Verify all parameters exist on event

verificationPatterns.pattern: Multiple concurrent failures each appear as discrete UI event entries
verificationPatterns.example: total 2 failure display on events

verificationPatterns.pattern: Non-failure errors (e.g. warnings/almost-panic) continue displaying after a failure-level event
verificationPatterns.example: Errors from relevant subsystem keep displaying after failure occurred

verificationPatterns.pattern: Cache window simulation: inject second failure within 2s prior + 2s delay of first
verificationPatterns.example: In cache of 2s prior 2s delay, simulate another failure (press state change)

verificationPatterns.pattern: HW/press failure triggers error event + red-X on wizard window
verificationPatterns.example: Error event displayed on UI and red x displayed on the wizard window

verificationPatterns.pattern: Closing and reopening wizard clears failure state
verificationPatterns.example: No failure event or red mark for the failure should displayed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Non-HW validation failure (wrong values) produces no event and no red mark
verificationPatterns.example: Start random wizard and failed the wizard on wrong values (Not HW issue or press failure) — No event displayed and no red mark for failure displayed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Warning message appears on UI when sensor value crosses near-empty threshold
verificationPatterns.example: Warning message about the relevant component display on UI for user

verificationPatterns.pattern: Error message appears after warning when condition worsens to empty
verificationPatterns.example: Error message appear after the warning message

verificationPatterns.pattern: Bypass of sensor suppresses the associated warning
verificationPatterns.example: Bypass conductivity and repeat step 1 — Warning not displayed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Pre-upgrade event emission check
verificationPatterns.example: Event issued as expected

verificationPatterns.pattern: SW upgrade success gate
verificationPatterns.example: SW upgrade finished successfully

verificationPatterns.pattern: Message center persistence of deprecated error after SW upgrade
verificationPatterns.example: On message center error still displayed even it removed from SW

verificationPatterns.pattern: Toast failure appearance fields
verificationPatterns.example: Toast color: Black(Failure), Event name: STATE_TRANSITION_TIMEOUT, Event time, Reported Component: Manager, Description

verificationPatterns.pattern: One toast per failure event; repeated failures produce additional toasts
verificationPatterns.example: Steps 1-3: first failure → 1 toast; second → 2 toasts; third → stacked view with 1 visible + 2 stacked

verificationPatterns.pattern: Tap toast stack to expand all
verificationPatterns.example: Tap on the event → stacked events expand → three toast events visible

verificationPatterns.pattern: Tap outside to collapse back to stacked view
verificationPatterns.example: Tap anywhere else on the screen → toasts return to stacked view

verificationPatterns.pattern: Swipe down on toast to expand description
verificationPatterns.example: Swipe down the middle event → event expanded and description fully visible

verificationPatterns.pattern: Swipe right to dismiss single toast
verificationPatterns.example: Swipe middle event to the right → middle event disappears, only two toasts remain

verificationPatterns.pattern: Click toast to open full view with text alignment check
verificationPatterns.example: Click on the event → full view opened and text is aligned

verificationPatterns.pattern: Teardown: restore default parameter and verify clean state transition
verificationPatterns.example: Change MechInit timeout to default → Go to Standby → Press reached Standby successfully

verificationPatterns.pattern: Events list presence check — verify named events appear with correct descriptions
verificationPatterns.example: Verify the following events is in the events list and the description is correct: BKT Subsystem: TEMP_PANIC_HIGH, CVC Subsystem: PRESSURE_PANIC_HIGH, ...

verificationPatterns.pattern: Negative presence check — verify excluded event does NOT appear in list
verificationPatterns.example: Verify the following event is not listed: PLC_FAILURE_STATE_CHANGE

verificationPatterns.pattern: State-change vs. event-only distinction — some signals produce events without state change
verificationPatterns.example: WHS Subsystem: Wait for RW_ROLL_FULL event (No State change)

verificationPatterns.pattern: UI filter verification — confirm severity filters (Failure, Error, Warning) function
verificationPatterns.example: Verify the Failure, Error, Warning filters works

verificationPatterns.pattern: Toggle button verification — confirm All/Unread toggle switches correctly
verificationPatterns.example: Verify All/Unread toggle button works

verificationPatterns.pattern: Expandable detail verification — click Technical Details and confirm content is correct
verificationPatterns.example: Click on 'Technical Details' — Verify technical details field expanded and the correct description is written inside

verificationPatterns.pattern: Search/filter verification — type partial event name or Event_id and confirm irrelevant events are filtered out, including localized input support
verificationPatterns.example: Verify that when starting to type the event name it's filtering out all not relevant events; Search shall be performed based on all textual localized values and Event_id

verificationPatterns.pattern: UI screenshot baseline check — open Messages Center and compare against reference image
verificationPatterns.example: Messages Center opened successfully and looks like this: !MessagesCenter.png|thumbnail!

verificationPatterns.pattern: Event counter badge on UI button reflects total active event count
verificationPatterns.example: The counter on the Messages button at the MainController is 3

verificationPatterns.pattern: Each event in overlay has correct severity color (Yellow=Warning, Red=Error, Black=Failure)
verificationPatterns.example: PRESSURE_HIGH: Yellow; SPM_TEMP_TOO_HIGH: Red; TEMP_PANIC_HIGH: Black

verificationPatterns.pattern: Each event in overlay shows correct component name and localized description
verificationPatterns.example: Component: LPH Cooling, Description: Relevant localization ID for PRESSURE_HIGH

verificationPatterns.pattern: Each event in overlay shows a correct timestamp/date
verificationPatterns.example: *Date:* Correct (verified for all three events)

verificationPatterns.pattern: All/Unread toggle filters overlay to only unread events and back
verificationPatterns.example: Switch to Unread: only 3 events visible (PRESSURE_HIGH, SPM_TEMP_TOO_HIGH, TEMP_PANIC_HIGH); switch back to All: all previous events visible

verificationPatterns.pattern: All/Unread toggle works correctly in combination with each severity filter
verificationPatterns.example: Step 11: Verify All/Unread toggle works when messages are filtered by All, Failure, Error, Warning

verificationPatterns.pattern: Severity filter shows only matching events and hides others; displayed count matches label
verificationPatterns.example: Failure filter: TEMP_PANIC_HIGH present, SPM_TEMP_TOO_HIGH absent, PRESSURE_HIGH absent, count matches label

verificationPatterns.pattern: Error severity filter isolates error-level events only
verificationPatterns.example: Error filter: SPM_TEMP_TOO_HIGH present, TEMP_PANIC_HIGH absent, PRESSURE_HIGH absent, count matches label

verificationPatterns.pattern: Warning severity filter isolates warning-level events only
verificationPatterns.example: Warning filter: PRESSURE_HIGH present, SPM_TEMP_TOO_HIGH absent, TEMP_PANIC_HIGH absent, count matches label

verificationPatterns.pattern: AWS upload destination validation
verificationPatterns.example: Verify data uploaded to correct folder in AWS (by press, date and type)

verificationPatterns.pattern: Post-upload local retention with status flag
verificationPatterns.example: After uploading, document still saved on press but status set to 'Uploaded'

verificationPatterns.pattern: No unbounded accumulation of pending-upload documents
verificationPatterns.example: Over time the number of IOs documents without status 'Uploaded' is not increased

verificationPatterns.pattern: Attribute parity across systems
verificationPatterns.example: Attributes and values for the event are equal in Press, Kibana and AWS

verificationPatterns.pattern: Data overload recovery with rate measurement
verificationPatterns.example: Stop uploader, bulk-create unuploaded docs, restart uploader, monitor upload rate and record throughput

verificationPatterns.pattern: Multi-level restart resilience
verificationPatterns.example: Execute Press SW restart, computer restart, and VM restart in sequence; verify upload resumes without issues after each

verificationPatterns.pattern: No bypass (value=0) reflects hardware detection: BIDInPlace matches physical state, BidID shows real S/N
verificationPatterns.example: BidInPlaceOverride=0 + BID installed → BIDInPlace=true, BidID=correct S/N

verificationPatterns.pattern: Force-not-in-place bypass (value=2) overrides hardware: BIDInPlace=false regardless of physical state, BidID returns sentinel '-'
verificationPatterns.example: BidInPlaceOverride=2 + BID installed → BIDInPlace=false, BidID='-'

verificationPatterns.pattern: Removing bypass (value=0) restores hardware detection: exported state matches actual physical absence
verificationPatterns.example: BidInPlaceOverride=0 + BID removed → BIDInPlace=false, BidID='-'

verificationPatterns.pattern: Force-in-place bypass (value=1) overrides hardware: BIDInPlace=true regardless of physical state, BidID returns sentinel '-' (no real detection)
verificationPatterns.example: BidInPlaceOverride=1 + BID absent → BIDInPlace=true, BidID='-'

verificationPatterns.pattern: Message index advance required after each bypass value change for new config to take effect
verificationPatterns.example: After setting BidInPlaceOverride, always advance OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.MEStation(X).ImportedData.MessageIndex before reading exported signals

verificationPatterns.pattern: BID physically present → BIDInPlace true and BidID populated with correct S/N
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.MEStation(X).ExportedData.BID(Y).Status.BIDInPlace = true; OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.MEStation(X).ExportedData.BID(X).Monitor.BidID = correct S/N

verificationPatterns.pattern: BID removed → BIDInPlace false and BidID set to sentinel value BADSERIALNUM
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.MEStation(X).ExportedData.BID(Y).Status.BIDInPlace = false; OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.MEStation(X).ExportedData.BID(Y).Monitor.BidID = BADSERIALNUM

verificationPatterns.pattern: Missing BID blocks Standby transition: UI button disabled with tooltip and AvailabilityStatus reflects reason code 236
verificationPatterns.example: Tooltip: 'BID (X*Y) not in place'; OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.MechInit.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Available = false; Reason[0].Reason = 236 (BID_NOT_IN_PLACE)

verificationPatterns.pattern: BID with incorrect/missing S/N → BIDInPlace true but BidID = BADSERIALNUM and BIMHV_BID_SN_IS_NOT_RECOGNIZED event fired in UI and logs with station number
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.MEStation(X).ExportedData.BID(Y).Status.BIDInPlace = true; Monitor.BidID = 'BADSERIALNUM'; BIMHV_BID_SN_IS_NOT_RECOGNIZED event in UI and logs including BID station number

verificationPatterns.pattern: Press prints successfully regardless of S/N validity (correct or incorrect/missing S/N both allow print)
verificationPatterns.example: Steps 5 and 7: bring press to ready, print job → Job is printed successfully

verificationPatterns.pattern: Replacing faulty BID with correct S/N via replacement wizard restores full detection: BIDInPlace true and BidID = correct S/N
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.MEStation(X).ExportedData.BID(Y).Status.BIDInPlace = true; OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.MEStation(X).ExportedData.BID(X).Monitor.BidID = correct S/N

verificationPatterns.pattern: Use BID replacement wizard for any BID install/remove operation during test steps (not hot-swap)
verificationPatterns.example: Steps 2, 4, 6, 8: Launch BID replacement wizard → perform physical swap → finish/close wizard

verificationPatterns.pattern: BidNotInPlace=true when FI open and no BIDHV comm (BID physically removed)
verificationPatterns.example: Remove BID from press, open FI (sensor not activated). PEX: IBL.BIDStationEntity.BidNotInPlace = true; App.MEStationPrintingEngineEntity.LefttInk/RightInk.NotInPlace = true; UI: black with yellow crossing line.

verificationPatterns.pattern: BidNotInPlace=true when FI closed and no BIDHV comm (BID absent but sensor active)
verificationPatterns.example: Do not install BID, close FI (sensor activated). PEX: IBL.BIDStationEntity.BidNotInPlace = true; App.MEStationPrintingEngineEntity.LefttInk/RightInk.NotInPlace = true; UI: black with yellow crossing line.

verificationPatterns.pattern: BidNotInPlace=true when FI open and BIDHV comm available (BID present but sensor inactive)
verificationPatterns.example: Install BID, open FI (sensor not active). PEX: IBL.BIDStationEntity.BidNotInPlace = true; App.MEStationPrintingEngineEntity.LefttInk/RightInk.NotInPlace = true; UI: black with yellow crossing line.

verificationPatterns.pattern: BidNotInPlace=false when FI closed and BIDHV comm available (both conditions met)
verificationPatterns.example: Keep BID in press, close FI (sensor active). PEX: IBL.BIDStationEntity.BidNotInPlace = false; App.MEStationPrintingEngineEntity.LefttInk/RightInk.NotInPlace = false; UI: ink color displayed, no crossing line.

verificationPatterns.pattern: UI reflects in-place state: color+no-crossing-line when in place, black+yellow-crossing-line when not
verificationPatterns.example: In place: BID displayed in assigned ink color, no crossing line. Not in place: BID marked black with yellow crossing line, no color.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Optional BID Engage wizard first-dialogue cross-check for each state
verificationPatterns.example: Optional test: BID Engage wizard, first dialogue, larger view — verify state reflected there too.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Override=2 suppresses in-place detection regardless of physical BID presence
verificationPatterns.example: Set BidInPlaceOverride.Value = 2 → BIDInPlace = false, Monitor.BidID = "-"

verificationPatterns.pattern: Override=0 enables hardware detection in detection-active states: BIDInPlace=true, BidID=correct S/N
verificationPatterns.example: Steps 5,7,9,11,16: Override=0 in Power Disabled/OFF/MechInit/Standby/Service → BIDInPlace = true, Monitor.BidID = correct S/N

verificationPatterns.pattern: Init state disables detection entirely; both Override=2 and Override=0 yield BIDInPlace=false, BidID='-'
verificationPatterns.example: Steps 2-3: Init state with Override=2 then Override=0 both produce BIDInPlace=false, Monitor.BidID='-'

verificationPatterns.pattern: Detection-active states (MechInit, Standby, Service): Override=2 causes press to fall to OFF and log BIMHV_BID_UNIT_NOT_DETECTED_AT_PRESS with correct BID station number
verificationPatterns.example: Steps 8,10,17: Override=2 in MechInit/Standby/Service → BIDInPlace=false, BidID='-', press falls to OFF, error in UI, log BIMHV_BID_UNIT_NOT_DETECTED_AT_PRESS

verificationPatterns.pattern: Detection-inactive states (Get Ready, Dynamic Ready, Print, Ready): Override=2 does not affect reported status; BIDInPlace stays true and BidID stays correct S/N, press proceeds normally
verificationPatterns.example: Steps 12-15: Override=2 during Get Ready/Dynamic Ready/Print/Ready → BIDInPlace=true, BidID=correct S/N, press reaches Ready/prints successfully

verificationPatterns.pattern: Paired-step state coverage: each press state tested with Override=2 first then Override=0 to bracket detection behavior
verificationPatterns.example: Steps 4-5 (Power Disabled), 6-7 (OFF), 8-9 (MechInit), 10-11 (Standby), 16-17 (Service): each state covered as two consecutive steps

verificationPatterns.pattern: OPC-UA exported status check
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.MEStation(X).ExportedData.BID(Y).Status.BIDInPlace = false

verificationPatterns.pattern: PEX IBL entity state check
verificationPatterns.example: PEX: IBL.BIDStationEntity.BidNotInPlace = true

verificationPatterns.pattern: PEX App entity ink NotInPlace check
verificationPatterns.example: PEX: App.MEStationPrintingEngineEntity.LefttInk/RightInk.NotInPlace = true

verificationPatterns.pattern: UI visual state check for BID removed/in-place
verificationPatterns.example: UI: removed BID is marked in black with yellow crossing line, color is not displayed

verificationPatterns.pattern: UI visual state check for BID fully in place
verificationPatterns.example: UI: removed BID is displayed in color of assigned ink, no crossing line

verificationPatterns.pattern: Truth-table exhaustion: all combinations of (BID detected, FI closed) verified
verificationPatterns.example: Steps 2-6 cover: (!detected,!FI), (!detected,FI), (detected,!FI), (detected,FI)

verificationPatterns.pattern: Brake release output verification (front and rear)
verificationPatterns.example: OCB_saPLC.OCB.gIos.BKT.BktTen.Output.BrakeReleaseFront.Value = True AND OCB_saPLC.OCB.gIos.BKT.BktTen.Output.BrakeReleaseRear.Value = True

verificationPatterns.pattern: Motor position known path: confirm last saved axis positions used and standby tension reached
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.BKT.SavedData.Tension.MechInit.LastAxisPosValid is set; gInterface.BKT.Comp.Tension.Ctrl.Out.Status.AtBldStandbyTen = True

verificationPatterns.pattern: Motor position unknown path: homing algorithm runs; verify standby tension achieved on home found, or timeout on home not found
verificationPatterns.example: 2.1 home found → gInterface.BKT.Comp.Tension.Ctrl.Out.Status.AtBldStandbyTen = True; 2.2 home not found → Tension timeout

verificationPatterns.pattern: Brake lock on power-off
verificationPatterns.example: BrakeReleaseFront.Value = False, BrakeReleaseRear.Value = False

verificationPatterns.pattern: Single-turn axis position persistence to SavedData
verificationPatterns.example: LastAxisPosFront and LastAxisPosRear written to OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.BKT.SavedData.Tension.MechInit

verificationPatterns.pattern: SavedData validity flag set True after save
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.BKT.SavedData.Tension.MechInit.LastAxisPosValid = True

verificationPatterns.pattern: BktTemp thread log sequence for successful FW update
verificationPatterns.example: Filter BktTemp thread for dimmer node name (e.g. 'CanOp_Multi9'); confirm sequence: 'CHStep: CanOp_Multi9, Boot - FW update needed=FwUpdateNeedCantChk, State 0' → 'Update request added to the service' → 'CHStep: CanOp_Multi9, Can Open - Operational, State 5' (appears twice)

verificationPatterns.pattern: FW update retry after mid-update interruption via emergency button
verificationPatterns.example: While FW upgrade is in progress, press emergency button; restart press SW and PLC; re-verify identical BktTemp log sequence confirming update completes on second restart

verificationPatterns.pattern: Read firmware version from tail of binary file via hex editor
verificationPatterns.example: Open BHV4.bin file by hex editor neo, scroll to the end of the file, remember the version that appears there

verificationPatterns.pattern: Auto-download triggers on PLC restart when binary version differs
verificationPatterns.example: Restart PLC → FW download started → Right SW Version installed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Correct SW version confirmed after successful download
verificationPatterns.example: Verify that SW downloaded and the SW version → Right SW Version installed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Download survives mid-update power interruption and completes on power restore
verificationPatterns.example: Shut down power during the SW update → Turn On the Power → Verify that SW downloading → Right SW Version installed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Print job from DFE validates end-to-end functionality post firmware update
verificationPatterns.example: Print job from DFE → Job from DFE printed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Confirm FW download triggered via log search
verificationPatterns.example: Verify SW downloaded and SW version in Log4view (search 'download')

verificationPatterns.pattern: Confirm correct SW version installed after download completes
verificationPatterns.example: Right SW Version installed (both steps)

verificationPatterns.pattern: Power-interruption resilience during FW update
verificationPatterns.example: Shut down power during SW update, turn power back on, verify SW resumes downloading and completes

verificationPatterns.pattern: End-to-end print validation after FW update
verificationPatterns.example: Print job from DFE after FW download completes, verify job prints successfully

verificationPatterns.pattern: Pre-download baseline capture
verificationPatterns.example: Check Current installed FW version and remember

verificationPatterns.pattern: FW version install verification after download
verificationPatterns.example: Verify that SW downloaded and the SW version / Right SW Version installed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Power-cut resilience during FW update
verificationPatterns.example: Shut down power during the SW update / Turn On the Power / Verify that SW downloading / Verify that SW downloaded and the SW version

verificationPatterns.pattern: Post-FW-update print job smoke test
verificationPatterns.example: Print job from DFE / Job from DFE printed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Post-FW-update Color Calibration pass check
verificationPatterns.example: Perform Color Calibration / Color calibration passed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Post-FW-update Focus Calibration pass check
verificationPatterns.example: Perform Focus Calibration / Focus calibration passed

verificationPatterns.pattern: Press SW launch success
verificationPatterns.example: Press SW launches successfully.

verificationPatterns.pattern: HMI progress bar visible during FW installation
verificationPatterns.example: Installation progress bar appears in HMI.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Post-install file integrity: PLC FW matches network source
verificationPatterns.example: File on PLC, C:\DriveFW\FW\Ax8000, is identical to S:\HP\16000. ... \Press\PLC\DriveFW\FW\Ax8000.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Functional smoke after FW update: print + calibrations succeed
verificationPatterns.example: All calibrations and print were performed successfully.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Recovery after mid-download power interruption: subsequent launch completes FW download and all smoke tests pass
verificationPatterns.example: Shut down main press power switch during the FW download … Turn on main press power switch. Launch press SW. … All calibrations and print were performed successfully.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Stress / multi-drive: all FW directories on PLC match network source
verificationPatterns.example: All files on PLC, C:\DriveFW\FW, are identical to S:\HP\16000. ... \Press\PLC\DriveFW\FW.

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check operation Available flag is true for stable idle states (OFF=3, STANDBY=6, READY=8)
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.Wash.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Available = true

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check operation Available flag is false with reason ILP_STATE_TRANSITION_IN_PROGRESS for transition states (MECHINIT=5, GetReady=7)
verificationPatterns.example:
OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.Wash.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Available = false
OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.Wash.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Reason[0].Reason = ILP_STATE_TRANSITION_IN_PROGRESS

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check operation Available flag is false with reason READY_REQUIRED for print-phase states (Pre-Print=9, Print=10, Post-Print=11)
verificationPatterns.example:
OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.Wash.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Available = false
OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.Wash.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Reason[0].Reason = READY_REQUIRED

verificationPatterns.pattern: Check operation Available flag is false with reason EXIT_SERVICE_REQUIRED for all service sub-modes (MNT, SEQ, EA)
verificationPatterns.example:
OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.Wash.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Available = false
OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.Wash.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Reason[0].Reason = EXIT_SERVICE_REQUIRED

verificationPatterns.pattern: Verify Drain availability mirrors Wash availability in every state
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.Drain.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Available = true/false (matches Wash result)

verificationPatterns.pattern: Countdown warning in main UI matches signal value
verificationPatterns.example: 3 minutes before AutoWash start a warning appears in main UI; displayed value equals OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.WEB.ExportedData.ILP.Monitor.MillingTimeoutRemainingTime

verificationPatterns.pattern: Same countdown warning visible inside open wizard dialog
verificationPatterns.example: Open ILP Wash wizard while warning is active; warning and remaining-time value still visible inside the dialog

verificationPatterns.pattern: Wizard reflects in-progress operation started outside it (buttons disabled with tooltip)
verificationPatterns.example: Play, Drain, and Close buttons unavailable with tooltip OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS when wash was triggered automatically

verificationPatterns.pattern: Progress bar color indicates active wash
verificationPatterns.example: Progress bar filled with blueish color during active wash

verificationPatterns.pattern: Wash timer counts down from expected maximum
verificationPatterns.example: Timer begins from 7 minutes and reduces to 0

verificationPatterns.pattern: Step markers reflect state via signal-driven logic
verificationPatterns.example: Not-started step grey; active step circular animation; completed step green V — driven by DrainRemainingTime, MillingTimeoutRemainingTime, WashRemainingTime signals

verificationPatterns.pattern: Warning dialog appears when attempting to unlock door that requires ILP wash
verificationPatterns.example: Press 'Unlock' button under PWS Priming title -> Observe new dialogue appears, with a warning about the length of ILP wash

verificationPatterns.pattern: Button disabled with reason code string when prerequisite process is in progress
verificationPatterns.example: PWS Priming 'Unlock' button is not available with a reason 'ILP_WASH_IN_PROGRESS'

verificationPatterns.pattern: Cross-wizard sync: same process remaining time displayed in both active wizards simultaneously
verificationPatterns.example: Same ILP Wash remaining time is displayed in both wizards, OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.WEB.ExportedData.ILP.Monitor.WashRemainingTime

verificationPatterns.pattern: Cross-wizard sync: same process stage displayed in both active wizards simultaneously
verificationPatterns.example: Same ILP Wash stage is displayed in both wizards, OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.WEB.ExportedData.ILP.Monitor.WashRemainingTime

verificationPatterns.pattern: Post-process state: press transitions to Service-Maintenance, gated action becomes available, process marked finished
verificationPatterns.example: Press should reach Service-Maintenance state; Priming door should be unlocked in Doors and Covers wizard; ILP Wash should be marked as finished in ILP Wash wizard

verificationPatterns.pattern: Bidirectional initiation: same in-progress UI state shown in wizard B when process was started from wizard A
verificationPatterns.example: Open ILP Wash wizard, press Play, wait for process to start, then open Doors and Covers wizard -> PWS Priming 'Unlock' button is not available with reason 'ILP_WASH_IN_PROGRESS'

verificationPatterns.pattern: Wizard play-button gating: button unavailable once wash starts
verificationPatterns.example: Press play button, wait for buzzer to end, press Play again — Play button is not available

verificationPatterns.pattern: Progress bar appears and advances during active wash
verificationPatterns.example: Progress bar appears and advances

verificationPatterns.pattern: Countdown timer decrements during wash
verificationPatterns.example: Wash time appears and reduces

verificationPatterns.pattern: Main UI mirrors wizard state: same progress bar titled 'Washing'
verificationPatterns.example: Same progress is displayed on progress bar, with a title 'Washing'

verificationPatterns.pattern: Main UI remaining-time matches signal value from wizard
verificationPatterns.example: Same process remaining time is displayed (OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.WEB.ExportedData.ILP.Monitor.WashRemainingTime)

verificationPatterns.pattern: Automatic wash trigger via timeout parameter as alternative setup path
verificationPatterns.example: Shorten OPCUAInterface.Subsystems.WEB.ImportedData.ILP.Param.AutoWashAfterFaultTime.Value and wait for automatic wash start

verificationPatterns.pattern: AvailabilityStatus.Available=false on blocking condition
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.Wash.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Available = false

verificationPatterns.pattern: Reason[0].Reason matches expected enum string for each blocking condition
verificationPatterns.example: OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.Wash.OperationData.AvailabilityStatus.Reason[0].Reason = TANK_LEVEL_PANIC_LOW

verificationPatterns.pattern: Assert blocking operation State=2 (IN_PROGRESS) before checking Wash availability for operation-conflict blocks
verificationPatterns.example: While OPCUAInterface.Global.Operations.WebFeedDryCorona.OperationData.State = 2 (IN_PROGRESS) → Wash Available=false, Reason=WHS_SYSTEM_WEB_FEED_IN_PROGRESS

verificationPatterns.pattern: Dual-pole simultaneous write for safety (EMS) signal injection
verificationPatterns.example: Set EmsInputPoleA.PE_FRNT_EXIT_ESTOP.Value=0 AND EmsInputPoleB.PE_FRNT_EXIT_ESTOP.Value=0 simultaneously

Close button is not available, with a tooltip OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS. Progress bar is filled with blueish color. Timer begins from 7 minutes, and reduces to 0. The timer is displayed in small font and is preceded by minus ("-") sign. Not started step is marked in grey, active step is marked with circular animation, completed step is marked with green "V".
